display.title: Tanya Shiur 28b: Rising at Chatzos, Loving Every Jew, and the Shofar's Call (Elul)
display.summary_short: A Yiddish shiur: Shulchan Aruch HaRav on rising at midnight, the end of Tanya 12 on the beinoni who repays harm with kindness, and an Elul talk on the shofar.
display.summary_long: Shiur 28b in Rabbi Yosef Goldstein's Yiddish Tanya series, recorded early in Elul. Part 1 continues the Alter Rebbe's Hilchos Hashkamas HaBoker, seifim 2 and 3: those who rise at midnight to mourn the Beis HaMikdash and the Shechinah in exile, why chatzos is a time of favor, and learning Torah until daybreak. Stories and teachings illustrate it: Rabbi Yisroel of Ruzhin's reading of 'I will fear no evil, for You are with me' after his release from prison, and Rabbi Akiva's rooster. Part 2 finishes Tanya chapter 12: the beinoni never lets a hateful thought about another Jew settle in his mind, and answers wrongs with kindness, as Yosef did with his brothers. Judging others favorably is illustrated by the Gemara's story of the worker whose employer said he had nothing to pay him. Part 3 is an Elul talk: the daily shofar is a wake-up call, like the town that bought a trumpet but forgot the water, and it leads to crowning Hashem as King on Rosh Hashanah.
display.lesson: Judge every Jew favorably and repay wrongs with kindness; and let the shofar of Elul wake you to real action in Torah and mitzvos.
